data:
The guide to the Comma tools for Grasshopper.
Getting startedInstall the plugins and find them in Grasshopper ComponentsEvery component of the Comma tab, generated from the plugin source Script OrganizerKeep a canvas clean: group colors, wires, scribbles and input tools

Every component sits in the Comma tab of Grasshopper, in one subcategory. This reference is generated from the plugin’s source code, so names, nicknames, inputs and outputs always match the build.
CurveCreate, divide, join, fillet and convert curves. (14) DataSort, group, branch and clean up lists and data trees. (12) DisplayDraw order, indices and directions of curves, points, surfaces and geometry in the viewport. (5) PlaneBuild frames and planes from curves, lines and other planes. (4) PointTest and sort points against planes and curves. (4) SurfaceExtract faces, extrude, untrim and unify surfaces and breps. (6) UtilParallel and coplanar tests, golden ratio tools, stair layout and document helpers. (9)

Create, divide, join, fillet and convert curves.
Component Nickname What it does DLine LnD Create a line segment defined by start point, tangent and length, optionally reversed or both sides XLine LnX Create a line segment along the X axis defined by start point and length, optionally reversed or both sides YLine LnY Create a line segment along the Y axis defined by start point and length, optionally reversed or both sides ZLine LnZ Create a line segment along the Z axis defined by start point and length, optionally reversed or both sides FlipX FX Flip a curve using vector unit X guide FlipY FY Flip a curve using vector unit Y guide FlipZ FZ Flip a curve using vector unit Z guide Divide Curve Plus Divide+ Divide a curve in points with additional options Extend On Surface ExtOnSrf Extend a curve on a surface Fillet Curve Plus Fillet+ Fillet a curve at multi parameters Join Curves Plus Join+ Join as many curves as possible being closer than a distance Convert Curve Convert Convert curves to polylines using angle and distance tolerances. Try Get Arc GArc Try to get a arc from a curve Try Get Circle GCircle Try to get a circle from a curve

data:
Divide a curve in points with additional options
Panel: Comma → Curve · Nickname: Divide+
data.inputs#Inputs:
Name Nickname Type Access Default Description Curve C Curve Item Curve to divide Distribution D Integer Item 0 Method to divide
Options: Equal distribution by number; Equal distribution by target length; By exact spacing (flexible first); By exact spacing (flexible middle); By exact spacing (flexible last); By exact spacing (flexible first and last); By exact spacings Length L Number Item 1000 Length of segments Count N Integer Item 10 Number of segments Exclude E Integer Item 0 Exclude options
Options: None (all included); First; Last; First and last; Second; Second to last; Second and second to last Spacings S Text Item "115 15*200 115" Exact spacing values for ‘By exact spacings’ mode.
Format: space-separated values, use N*L for N repetitions of length L.
Example: “115 15*200 115”
Remainder is left at the end.
data.outputs#Outputs: Name Nickname Type Access Description Points P Point List Division points Tangents T Vector List Tangent vectors at division points Parameters t Number List Parameter values at division points

data:
Sort, group, branch and clean up lists and data trees.
Component Nickname What it does Branch Index Branch # Retrieves all items in a specified branch by index Cull Ends CullE Cull (remove) first end last items from a list Group By Keys GrpKeys Groups items from a primary list into branches based on similar string keys, and groups corresponding items from additional lists into the same branches. Branch-aware: grouping applies per input branch. Partition List Plus Partition+ Partition a list into sub-lists with overlap Change Case Case Changes text case similar to Microsoft Word: Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word, tOGGLE cASE Sort Area SArea Sort geometries by area Sort Length SLn Sort curves by length Sort Volume SVol Sort geometries by volume Sort X SortX Sort geometries by X coordinate Sort Y SortY Sort geometries by Y coordinate Sort Z SortZ Sort geometries by Z coordinate Sort By Type SortByType Sort Rhino objects into buckets by geometry type

data:
Parallel and coplanar tests, golden ratio tools, stair layout and document helpers.
Component Nickname What it does Stair Layout StLay Generates a stair profile using a 3D guide curve Select In Document SelDoc Select object in Rhino document Are Planes Coplanar? Co-Planar? Checks if two planes are co-planar within tolerance. Are Planes Parallel? PlParallel? Checks if two planes are parallel within an angle tolerance. Are Vectors Parallel? VecParallel? Checks if two vectors are parallel within an angle tolerance. Group Document Objects GrpObj Group specified document objects together Golden Divide GoldDiv Divides a curve into golden sections by arc length (a/b = φ). Golden Rectangle GoldRec Creates a golden-ratio rectangle on a plane from an X interval. Golden Triangle GoldTri Create a golden-ratio triangle on a plane from an X interval

Checks if two planes are co-planar within tolerance.
Panel: Comma → Util · Nickname: Co-Planar?
data.inputs#Inputs: Name Nickname Type Access Default Description Plane A A Plane Item First vector. Plane A B Plane Item Second vector. Tolerance Tol Number Item RhinoDoc.ActiveDoc?.ModelAbsoluteTolerance ?? 1e-2 Distance tolerance Angle Tolerance ATol Number Item RhinoDoc.ActiveDoc?.ModelAngleToleranceDegrees?? 1.0 Angular tolerance in degrees (°)
data.outputs#Outputs: Name Nickname Type Access Description Relation R Integer Item 1 = coplanar & co-direction (normals aligned), -1 = coplanar & opposite (normals reversed), 0 = not coplanar.

data.tidy-a-canvas#Tidy a canvas: Group some components (Ctrl+G) and name the group with a prefix such as r_inputs. With Script Organizer’s automatic mode on, the group takes the color of its prefix and the wires that leave the group fade. Open Comma → Settings… to change the prefix colors or turn the automatic modes off. See Script Organizer for every feature.
data.use-a-component#Use a component: Open the Comma tab in the Grasshopper ribbon. Components are grouped in panels: Curve, Data, Display, Plane, Point, Surface and Util. Drag a component onto the canvas, or double-click the canvas and type its name or nickname (for example Divide+). Hover over an input or output to read its description. Every component of the plugin is also listed in the component reference, with all inputs, outputs and options. A component that reports a problem turns orange or red. Click the balloon in its corner to read the message.

data: Comma for Grasshopper is two separate plugins. Install the one you need, or both.
data.check-that-it-loaded#Check that it loade:
Open Grasshopper. You should see:
a Comma tab in the component ribbon (Comma Components); a Comma menu in Grasshopper’s menu bar and a row of color, wire and Opacity controls at the end of the canvas toolbar (Comma Script Organizer). If a plugin does not show up, check the Rhino command line for load errors and make sure the zip was unblocked and extracted completely.
data.comma-components#Comma Components:
Download the zip that matches your Rhino from the Releases page:
Rhino File Rhino 7 (Windows) Comma.GH.Components-v-net48.zip Rhino 8 (Windows) Comma.GH.Components-v-net7.0-windows.zip Rhino 8 (Mac) Comma.GH.Components-v-net7.0.zip On Windows, right-click the zip, choose Properties, tick Unblock and click OK. Windows blocks downloaded .gha files otherwise and Grasshopper will not load them.
Extract the zip into a folder inside Grasshopper’s Components folder (in Grasshopper: File → Special Folders → Components Folder).
Restart Rhino.
The zip holds Comma.GH.Components.gha and Comma.Core.dll. Keep them together in the same folder.
data.comma-script-organizer#Comma Script Orga: Comma Script Organizer is a Rhino 8 package named Comma_GH_ScriptOrganizer, built for Grasshopper on Windows. Install it from Rhino’s Package Manager (type PackageManager in the Rhino command line and search for Comma_GH_ScriptOrganizer), then restart Rhino.

data:
Comma Script Organizer keeps a Grasshopper canvas readable while you work. It adds a Comma menu to Grasshopper’s menu bar and a row of buttons to the canvas toolbar, and it works on the active Grasshopper document.
Color GroupColor groups from the prefix of their name, or with the canvas color buttons Fix ParamsShow parameter names instead of icons on every new parameter Fix WireFade the wires that cross from one group to another ScribbleLabel groups with scribbles and resize them Input toolsClear or internalise the inputs of selected components Ctrl+Alt copy without wiresDrag-copy components without their input wires Settings and shortcutsAutomatic modes, prefix colors, canvas opacity and keyboard shortcuts ChangelogWhat changed in each version
data.automatic-and-manual-modes#Automatic and:
Three features have an Auto mode that is on by default: Color Group, Fix Params and Fix Wire. In automatic mode they react to what you do on the canvas. Each also has a Run Once command in the Comma menu that works on the whole document at the time you choose, whether the automatic mode is on or not, and a Reset Default command that undoes the effect on the selected objects (or on everything when nothing is selected).
Settings are stored in Grasshopper’s own settings, so they are kept between sessions.

data: All notable changes to the Comma_GH_ScriptOrganizer package, newest first.
data.010--2026-03-30#0.1.0 — 2026-03-30: Initial release: automatic group coloring by name prefix, canvas/panel color settings, and fainted cross-group wires.
data.110--2026-03-31#1.1.0 — 2026-03-31: Renamed the plugin/assembly from Comma.GH.ColorGroups to Comma.GH.ScriptOrganizer. Added the Scribble tool: label selected groups from their name, and increase/decrease scribble font size. Simplified Internalize Selected Inputs. Improved Auto Reference and Fix Wire behavior.
data.2610--2026-08-02#26.1.0 — 2026-08-02: Bounded the Scribble tool’s font size to the range [5, 100]. Removed the Auto Reference feature (creating Param > Geometry components from the Rhino selection) and its “Layer Info” setting. Fixed the canvas toolbar’s color and wire-display button groups swapping places when one of the two was rebuilt after the other. Auto Reference now creates a Grasshopper document if none is open yet (folded in from the unpublished 1.2.0 line). Settings dialog now applies feature toggles (Auto, Remove Prefix, Debug, etc.) before applying color changes, so color updates see the correct flags. Fix Params and Fix Wire now refresh the canvas immediately after running. Versioning scheme moved to 26.1.0 going forward.
data.2611--2026-08-19#26.1.1 — 2026-08-19: Added an Opacity dropdown (100% / 70% / 50%) to the canvas toolbar for adjusting the Grasshopper editor window’s transparency.
data.2612--2026-09-14#26.1.2 — 2026-09-14: Opacity dropdown now behaves like Grasshopper’s native Zoom Factor control: it accepts a typed custom percentage (clamped to 20%–100%) in addition to the 100% / 70% / 50% presets, normalizes the text to “NNN%” on commit, and reverts on Escape. Fixed the Opacity dropdown showing two overlapping/flickering tooltips on hover.
data.2613--2026-10-07#26.1.3 — 2026-10-07: Color Group is now undoable (Ctrl+Z) in both manual and automatic mode: recoloring/renaming a group, Run Once, Reset Default (all/selected), and the canvas color swatch buttons (which create a new group) all properly record undo. Multiple groups changed in a single action share one combined undo record, so one Ctrl+Z reverts the whole action instead of only the last group touched. Scribble (Label Groups, and the font Size +/- buttons) is now undoable for the same reason: creating, removing, and re-adding scribbles, and updating group membership, previously left nothing on the undo stack. Restored the Default/Faint/Hidden wire-display button icons, which were missing from the previous release.
data.2614--2026-10-12#26.1.4 — 2026-10-12: New “Color Only (no text)” option in the Color Group dialog: the canvas color buttons create groups with no name, carrying only the color. Unnamed groups whose color matches a preset are no longer reset to the default color by auto mode. When a group is selected, the canvas color buttons now recolor that group (one undo step for all selected groups) instead of creating a new group around it.
data.2615--2026-10-26#26.1.5 — 2026-10-26: Added “Ctrl+Alt Copy Without Wires” (Comma menu toggle, on by default): when drag-copying with Alt, holding Ctrl as the mouse is released makes the copies come out without the input wires from the original sources. Wires between the copied objects themselves are kept. Fixed Ctrl+Alt copy handlers staying attached to a closed document or being hooked to the canvas more than once.
data.2616--2026-10-27#26.1.6 — 2026-10-27: Republished: 26.1.5 was built without the 26.1.4 changes (Color Only option, recolor selected groups). This release contains both.

data: Color Group colors Grasshopper groups for you. A group is colored from the prefix of its name: the text before the first underscore, including the underscore. A group named r_inputs has the prefix r_.
data.automatic-mode#Automatic mode:
With Auto on, a group is recolored when you rename it, and when groups are added to the canvas or pasted (all of them in one undo step). Color-only changes do not trigger it, so a color you set by hand stays.
A group is left untouched when:
its name has no underscore, for example inputs; its prefix is not in the prefix table. A group with no name at all gets the default group color, unless it already has a prefix color.
data.canvas-color-buttons#Canvas color button:
The canvas toolbar has one color swatch per prefix. Select some objects and click a swatch to put them in a new group of that color. If a group is selected, the swatch recolors that group (and every selected group) instead of creating a new one, in one undo step.
By default the new group is named from the prefix. Two options in Settings change this:
Remove Prefix: the leading segment is stripped from the name (r_references becomes references). Color Only (no text): the new group has no name and carries only the color. Unnamed groups that have a prefix color are not reset to the default color by automatic mode.
data.commands#Commands: Command in Comma → Color Group What it does Run One Recolors all groups in the active document now. Reset Default Resets the selected groups, or all groups when nothing is selected, to the default group color. Every color change can be undone with Ctrl+Z, and one action that changes several groups is a single undo step.
data.default-prefix-colors#Default prefix col: Prefix Color (R, G, B) i_ green (125, 217, 98) s_ orange (224, 145, 81) g_ off-white (245, 243, 237) c_ beige (235, 227, 206) o_ light blue (160, 218, 242) r_ red (242, 63, 63) y_ yellow (247, 244, 64) u_ purple (208, 115, 230) od_ gray (97, 97, 97) The prefixes have no built-in meaning: use them however your team names things. Change, add or remove prefixes in Settings. A prefix you type without a trailing underscore gets one added.

data:
Grasshopper copies objects when you drag with Alt held down, and the copies keep their input wires to the original sources. With Ctrl+Alt Copy Without Wires you can drag-copy and leave the wires behind.
Select the objects and start dragging them with Alt held down. Hold Ctrl as you release the mouse button. The copies come out without the input wires from the original sources. Wires between the copied objects themselves are kept, and one Undo removes the copies.
Without Ctrl, Alt drag-copy behaves exactly as in Grasshopper. The feature is a toggle in Comma → Ctrl+Alt Copy Without Wires (on by default). Only drag-copies are affected: pasting and dropping from the toolbar are left alone.
Parameters such as Number Slider or Curve show an icon by default. Fix Params switches them to show their name instead, so a canvas full of parameters stays readable.
data.automatic-mode#Automatic mode: With Auto on, every parameter you add to the canvas is set to name display. Parameters that were already in the document are not touched until you run the command.
data.commands#Commands: Command in Comma → Fix Params What it does Run Once Sets name display on every parameter in the active document. Reset Default Puts the selected parameters (or all of them when nothing is selected) back on Grasshopper’s default display mode. Turn Print Log on in Settings to see in the Rhino command line which parameters were changed.

data: Fix Wire fades the wires that connect objects living in different groups, so the wires inside a group stand out and the canvas looks calmer.
data.automatic-mode#Automatic mode: With Auto on, Fix Wire runs after every solution, once all the wires are settled.
data.canvas-wire-buttons#Canvas wire buttons: Three buttons on the canvas toolbar set the wire display of the selected parameters and components that have at least one incoming wire: Default, Faint and Hidden.
data.commands#Commands: Command in Comma → Fix Wire What it does Run One Fades the cross-group wires in the active document now. Reset Default Resets the selected wires (or all of them when nothing is selected) to the default display.
data.how-it-decides#How it decides:
Only objects that belong to at least one group are looked at. For each input, Fix Wire checks the objects its wires come from: when none of them shares a group with the input’s object, the input’s wires are faded. If at least one source shares a group with it, the wires keep the default display.
If you change the display of a wire yourself (right-click menu or the canvas wire buttons), Fix Wire stops managing that wire and leaves your choice alone.

data: Two commands in the Comma menu work on the inputs of the components you have selected.
data.clear-selected-inputs#Clear Selected Inp: Clears the persistent data stored in the selected inputs and disconnects their wires. Use it to reset a component to an empty state.
data.internalise-selected-inputs#Internalise: Copies the data that arrives through wires (or from Rhino references) into the input’s own persistent storage, and disconnects the wires. The component then keeps working without its former sources, and a parameter that referenced Rhino geometry no longer depends on the Rhino document. It does the same as Grasshopper’s built-in Internalise command, but for all selected inputs at once.

data:
Scribbles turn the name of a group into a label on the canvas.
Command in Comma → Scribble What it does Label Groups (Ctrl+Shift+L) For each selected group, creates a scribble from the group’s name, places it at the group’s top-left corner and adds it to the group. Size + Increases the font size of the selected scribbles by one step. Size - Decreases the font size of the selected scribbles by one step. The font size is limited to the range 5 to 100. Creating, removing and resizing scribbles can all be undone with Ctrl+Z.

data.canvas-toolbar#Canvas toolbar:
At the end of Grasshopper’s canvas toolbar you find:
one color swatch per prefix (see Color Group); the Default, Faint and Hidden wire buttons (see Fix Wire); an Opacity box that sets the transparency of the Grasshopper window: pick 100%, 70% or 50%, or type your own percentage between 20% and 100%. Press Esc to cancel what you typed.
data.keyboard-shortcuts#Keyboard shortcuts: The commands of the Comma menu (Run Once, Reset Default, Label Groups, Size +/-, Clear and Internalise Selected Inputs and the Ctrl+Alt toggle) are registered with Grasshopper’s keyboard shortcut system, so you can assign your own shortcuts to them in Grasshopper’s shortcut settings. Label Groups has Ctrl+Shift+L by default.
data.settings-dialog#Settings dialog:
Open Comma → Settings… (the dialog is titled Comma Settings).
Section Options Color Group Auto, Remove Prefix, Color Only (no text), Print Log Fix Params Auto, Print Log Fix Wire Auto, Print Log Colors The canvas color, the panel color, the default group color and the Prefix Groups table (prefix and color). + Add adds a prefix, Defaults restores the original prefixes. Click OK to apply and Cancel to close without changes. Print Log writes what a feature did to the Rhino command line, which helps when something does not behave as you expect.
